mgmt_bio.text: Cameron M. Bready is chief executive officer and a member of the board of directors of Global Payments Inc. (NYSE: GPN), the Atlanta-based payments technology and software company. He joined Global Payments in 2014 as senior executive vice president and chief financial officer, responsible for global financial operations, and served as president and chief operating officer from 2019, overseeing worldwide merchant solutions, global operations, risk management, product and real estate. He was named president and chief executive officer in succession to Jeffrey S. Sloan effective June 1, 2023, joining the board at that time. Before Global Payments he was executive vice president and CFO of ITC Holdings Corp., vice president of finance at Northeast Utilities and senior vice president of Mirant Corporation.

sentences.text: In January 2026 Global Payments disclosed two senior departures: Chief Accounting Officer David Sheffield gave notice of retirement effective March 1, 2026, and Chief Administrative Officer David Green resigned for good reason, ceasing to serve in that role as of January 9, 2026.

Nichole Viviani was hired as Chief People, Culture and Change Officer effective January 9, 2026, becoming an executive officer on January 29, and Jennifer Bozeman Whyte, a company finance veteran since 2007, succeeded Sheffield as Chief Accounting Officer from March 1, 2026.

In February 2026, after engagement with Elliott Investment Management, the board added Vivek Sankaran as an independent director, with CEO Cameron Bready framing priorities as integrating Worldpay and advancing commerce solutions.

thesis_pillars.text: Global Payments Inc. (NYSE: GPN) has reshaped its portfolio: it completed the Worldpay acquisition and the divestiture of Issuer Solutions, becoming a pure-play commerce solutions provider with three segments, Enterprise, Platforms and SMB. Full-year 2026 guidance calls for normalized constant-currency adjusted net revenue growth of 4-5%, adjusted EPS of $13.60-$13.80 and about 150 basis points of operating margin expansion. Management describes capital allocation as a central pillar of the investment thesis, with more than $2 billion of returns planned in 2026 and $7.5 billion over 2025-2027. Growth investment is concentrated in AI and the Genius platform, supporting new client wins and product launches.
